items.prompt: Carlos is proud of ___ daughter, who has just graduated.

explanation.en: The possessive agrees with the owner (Carlos is a man), not with the daughter.
explanation.es: Concuerda con el poseedor: Carlos → his, aunque «hija» sea femenino.

optionNotes.en: Her would mean the daughter of another woman.
Correct: the owner is Carlos, so his.
Their would need more than one owner.

items.prompt: I twisted ___ ankle playing football, so I can't run this week.

explanation.en: Body parts take a possessive determiner in English.
explanation.es: En español decimos «el tobillo»; en inglés, my ankle.

optionNotes.en: The is the Spanish pattern but is not used with your own body parts.
Correct: possessive determiner before a noun.
Mine is a pronoun and cannot come before a noun.

items.prompt: Nobody helped him; he built the whole website ___.

explanation.en: Himself is used for emphasis, to show he did it alone.

optionNotes.en: Him is an object pronoun and does not work here.
Itself would refer to the website, not to the person.

items.prompt: Which of these coats is yours? — This one is ___.

explanation.en: No noun follows the gap, so we need the possessive pronoun mine.

optionNotes.en: My must be followed by a noun.
Me is an object pronoun, not a possessive.

items.prompt: Ana introduced me to a friend of ___ from university.

explanation.en: After a friend of we use the possessive pronoun: a friend of hers.
explanation.es: «Una amiga suya» = a friend of hers.

optionNotes.en: After of, we use hers, not the determiner her.
Correct: a friend of + possessive pronoun.
She is a subject pronoun and is never used after of.
